subject: Hosted API throughput anomaly - customer escalation (FastRetail)
messages:
From: Kevin Li <kevin.li@fastretail.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+escalations@fastretail.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 spikes and throughput drop on Hosted API

Rishi,

We're seeing significant regressions in p95/p99 latency and a large drop in token-per-second throughput on the Hosted API starting Nov 11th (roughly 18:00 UTC). Our customer-facing endpoints that used to average ~1,200 tps are now at ~720 tps during steady-state and p99 latency has jumped from ~420ms to >1.2s on multiple routes. Error rate has also increased (~1.4% 5xx). This is impacting order processing at peak and causing queueing in our downstream systems.

We haven't changed our client behavior. Our SRE pulled request IDs and sample traces for you (included below). Can you confirm if Redwood made any runtime/quant/kernel changes around Nov 10-12? We need an urgent remediation plan, ETA, and whether you can roll back any change that could be the cause.

Sample request ids: fr-req-20261112-88a1, fr-req-20261112-8b2c
Attached: customer_logs_snippet.txt (excerpt), latency_graphs_20261113.png

Please escalate — this is causing significant customer impact.

Thanks,
Kevin Li
Head of Platform Engineering
FastRetail

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Li <kevin.li@fastretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, ops+escalations@fastretail.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spikes and throughput drop on Hosted API

Kevin — thanks for the heads up and the sample ids. I'm escalating internally and we've opened INF-9345 to track this.

Immediate plan:
- Internal triage call in 30 minutes with runtime + kernel engineers (invites sent).
- We will snapshot the rolling hosts that served the request ids you supplied and run a targeted profile.
- If we confirm a rollout correlated with the regression we can roll that change back within our maintenance window tonight.

Can you confirm windows of highest impact (timestamps + a representative request body) and whether you can tolerate a short failback (~5–10 minutes) to a pinned model variant if we ask? We'll also propose a small credit given the impact.

I know this is urgent — I'm personally owning this and will keep you updated every 2 hours until resolved.

— Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: kevins@fastretail.com, ops+escalations@fastretail.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Sudden p95/p99 spikes and throughput drop on Hosted API

Adding initial findings from a quick profile against the sample request ids and a small set of production hosts:

Summary:
- We rolled QuantProfile v2.1 on Nov 10 at 02:00 UTC (canary -> full rollout by Nov 11).
- Profiling shows token-per-second throughput on the int8 quantized path dropped ~35–45% for sequences >256 tokens compared to v2.0.
- p95/p99 regressed on routes that commonly use continuous batching and long KV cache lifetimes.
- Kernel selector appears to prefer a new int8 fused attention kernel that has an optimal case for short sequences but has higher per-token overhead for longer sequences when batching is wide. That overhead interacts poorly with our continuous-batching policy, increasing queueing latency.

Attachments: profile_dump_quant_v2.1.tar.gz (contains nvprof traces + timeline), gpu_traces_20261114.csv

Short-term options:
1) Rollback QuantProfile to v2.0 (fastest; will restore previous kernel selection and throughput).
2) Pin kernel selector to legacy-fp32-path for affected hosts (requires kernel flag change, small risk).
3) Tune batching window to reduce wide-batch cases for long sequences (mitigation, but needs careful rollout).

I recommend option 1 for immediate recovery (we can revert in <30min and monitor). While rolling back we'll run a canary of option 2/3 on a small host pool to find a longer-term fix.

I'll stand by for the bridge.

— Marissa
Sr. Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+escalations@fastretail.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Sudden p95/p99 spikes and throughput drop on Hosted API

Numbers from the prod hosts we sampled (median across 6 hosts):
- pre-v2.1 (Nov 9): token/sec: 1186, p95: 0.42s, p99: 0.74s, 5xx: 0.2%
- post-v2.1 (Nov 12): token/sec: 710, p95: 1.02s, p99: 1.45s, 5xx: 1.4%

Observations:
- The int8 fused kernel increases CPU side dispatch overhead for long sequences; GPU utilization per batch increased but actual effective throughput reduced because of smaller useful kernel launches per GPU cycle.
- KV cache hit-rate looks unchanged, but our batching window is amplifying the per-request overhead.

Canary plan: rollback v2.1 in small pool tonight (2 hosts), verify tps+latency restore, then roll back globally. If rollback is blocked we will instead set kernel_selector=legacy-fp32 for the affected route group and expand canary.

I'll prepare the rollback playbook and a runbook note for SRE.

— Jonas
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent - FastRetail impact (exec escalation)

Team — copying execs for visibility. Kevin is reporting a customer-facing outage pattern caused by our recent inference runtime update. We need a customer-facing message with a clear remediation ETA and a proposed credit.

Actions I expect by EOD (PST):
- Rishi: Owning customer comms — propose text and credit amount (preapproved up to $25k for strategic accounts).
- Marissa/Jonas: Rollback plan and timeline (if rollback is the chosen path, include risk statement and rollback steps).
- Ops: Prepare postmortem template and timeline for weekly updates.

We should also consider pausing any further runtime rollouts until postmortem complete. Keep me posted every 2 hours.

— Evelyn
VP, Customer Success (interim)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Li <kevin.li@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, ops+escalations@fastretail.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 18:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API throughput anomaly - customer escalation (FastRetail)

Kevin — follow-up from our investigation and actions taken. Thank you for your patience.

What we found:
- The rollout of QuantProfile v2.1 on Nov 10 changed kernel selection heuristics for the int8 path. For longer sequences with wide continuous batching this resulted in higher per-token CPU/GPU dispatch overhead and a net drop in effective token-per-second.

What we did (executed 2026-11-15 02:30 UTC):
- Per Marissa/Jonas recommendation we rolled QuantProfile back to v2.0 across the affected host pool during a controlled maintenance window.
- Ran canary verification on a subset of production hosts (4 hosts) for 40 minutes. Observed token/sec return to ~1,150 and p95/p99 returned to baseline within the monitoring window.
- We have paused further automatic rollout of QuantProfile releases pending a full postmortem and regression test additions.

Next steps and timeline:
- Immediate: Continue monitoring for 48 hours; we'll provide an hourly summary for the first 6 hours, then 4x daily updates thereafter.
- Short-term: We will run an internal kernel-selector audit and add sequence-length-aware unit tests to prevent similar regressions (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Compensation: We're issuing a service credit for the impacted window. Proposed credit: $18,000. Please confirm if that is acceptable and we'll issue through the billing contact.

Attachments: latency_graphs_20261113.png (customer visualization), profile_dump_quant_v2.1.tar.gz (for your reference), gpu_traces_20261114.csv

Apologies for the disruption. We're treating this as a Sev-1 and will publish a full postmortem within 7 business days. I'll send the customer-facing summary after I hear back on the credit.

— Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
